questions.question:
**Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.**

Restricted
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 1) Copious**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**restricted**" means** limited, confined, or restrained**. It implies a lack of freedom or a limitation on something.

 
 
• For example, if someone has restricted access to a certain area, it means their access is limited or controlled.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, "**copious**" means **abundant, plentiful, or extensive. **It refers to a large quantity or amount of something. For instance, if there is a copious amount of rainfall, it means there is a significant and abundant rainfall.
 
 
• Example sentence using "**restricted**" - The company has **restricted **the use of social media during working hours.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **1) Copious**, which represents the opposite meaning of "**restricted**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2) Circumscribed** is similar in meaning to "restricted" as it also implies something being limited or restricted. It means to confine within limits or boundaries.

 
 
• For example: The project's budget was circumscribed, leaving no room for additional expenses.
 
 
 
• **Option 3) Capped** means to set a limit or put a maximum restriction on something. While it shares some similarity with "restricted," it specifically refers to imposing a maximum limit.
 
 
• For example: The maximum number of participants for the workshop is capped at 50.
 
 
 
• **Option 4) Finite** means having a definite or limited duration, extent, or quantity. It indicates something having an endpoint or being bounded. Although it is related to limitation, it is not the opposite of "restricted."
 
 
• For example: Our resources are finite, so we need to use them wisely.

questions.question:
**Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.**

She said to her, "Please pay attention to the details."

options.text: She commanded her for paying attention to the details.
She requested her that to pay attention to the details.
She requests her that pay attention to the details.
She requested her to pay attention to the details.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **She requested her to pay attention to the details.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in** Direct Speech** and is in an imperative sentence. As per the given instructions, we have to change it into **Indirect Speech.**
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
• The conjunction 'to' will be added and comma and inverted commas will be removed.
 
• In the Indirect speech 'said to' will be changed into 'requested' because the person is making a request.
 
• The indirect speech will begin like **'She requested her to.'**
 
• Now we have to change the reported speech.
 
• According to the rules of grammar, after 'to' we have to use 'V1 (pay).'
 
• Finally, the indirect speech is **'****She requested her to pay attention to the details.'**
 
• So, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *She requested her to pay attention to the details.*

questions.question:

__
 
• The word "**efficacy**" refers to** the ability or effectiveness of achieving a desired result or producing a desired effect**. It suggests the capability or power of something to bring about a successful outcome.

 
 
• For example, if a medicine has high efficacy, it means it is effective in treating a particular condition. 
 
 
 
• On the other hand, "**efficiency**" is **the quality or state of being efficient, which means achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or resources**. It implies the ability to accomplish tasks or goals in a timely and effective manner. For instance, if a process or system is efficient, it means it is well-organized and optimized for productivity.
 
• Example sentence using "**efficacy**":
 
 
• The **efficacy **of the new cleaning product in removing stains was impressive.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** 2) Efficiency**, which is a synonym of "**efficacy**" as it implies effectiveness, productivity, and accomplishing tasks with minimal wastage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) Impotence **means powerlessness or inability to take action or achieve results. It is the opposite of efficacy and does not have a similar meaning.
 
• **Option 3) Ineptness** refers to a lack of skill or competence. It is not synonymous with efficacy as it suggests incompetence or inability rather than effectiveness.
 
• **Option 4) Futility **means the state of being pointless, useless, or ineffective. It is opposite in meaning to efficacy and does not share a similar meaning.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the (bracketed) part of the sentence. In case of no improvement select the option 'No improvement'.**

The play was (either as funny or as) disturbing as Shivang told it was.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Neither as funny nor as.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence **"The play was (either as funny or as) disturbing as Shivang told it was" **contains an error in the use of correlative conjunctions.
 
• **Correlative conjunctions **are used to join words or groups of words that have equal importance in a sentence.
 
• In this case, the correlative conjunction** "either...or" **is incorrectly used. It should be replaced with **"neither...nor" **to convey the intended meaning.
 
• **"Neither...nor"** is **used to present two negative options or choices.**
 
 
• Sentence with the improved option: The play was **neither as funny nor as**__ disturbing as Shivang told it was.
 
 
 
• In this corrected sentence, the use of** "neither...nor"** properly balances the comparison between the play's level of funniness and its level of disturbance. It ensures that both aspects are presented as negative or not as expected.
 
• The other options provided, such as** "either as funny nor as" **and **"neither as funny or as," **are grammatically incorrect and do not convey the intended meaning. Therefore, **option 1, "neither as funny nor as," **is the correct choice.

__**Correct Sentence**__: *The play was __**(neither as funny nor as)**__ disturbing as Shivang told it was.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

He writes a paper every weekend.

options.text: A paper is written by him every weekend.
A paper is been written by him every weekend.
A paper was been written by him every weekend.
A paper was written by him every weekend.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **A paper is written by him every weekend.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The above-given sentence is in the active voice. We need to change it into **passive voice.**
 
• Let's look at the conversion:-
 
 
• The subject** 'He'** becomes the object **'him'** of the passive voice.
 
• The object **'****a paper****'** becomes the subject of the passive voice.
 
• Simple present tense changes in the following manner:-
 
• Active Voice - (do/does + V1) or (V1 s/es)
 
• Passive Voice - is/am/are + V3​
 
• The simple present tense changes according to the above-mentioned structure.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

Therefore, the correct passive voice is *A paper is written by him every weekend.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use the third form of the verb in the passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.

• Therefore, the correct answer is** 4) contaminated,** as it accurately describes the state of the water being polluted or compromised by harmful substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

They know they will face / either a swift backlash / or deafening silence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 1) No error.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence does not contain any grammatical errors. It is grammatically correct and effectively conveys the intended meaning.
 
 
• *"They know they will face either a swift backlash or deafening silence."*
 
 
 
• In this sentence, all parts are properly constructed and there are no grammatical inconsistencies or errors.
 
• The use of "either...or" is appropriate, and the sentence presents two possible outcomes that the subject is aware of.
 
• The conjunction "or" is correctly used to connect the two alternatives.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is indeed **1) No error.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] Confusion Points__ **

 
• In most cases, the use of **"a" or "the"** (indefinite or definite articles) depends on whether the noun is **countable **or **uncountable**, and whether we are referring to something specific. 

 
 
• For instance, in the case of the sentences**: "either a dog or a cat", "either a queen or a king", and "either a red card or a black card", all the nouns (dog, cat, queen, king, red card, black card) **are **countable **and not specific. Therefore, we require "a" before each of these nouns.
 
 
 
• In the case of '**deafening silence**', the **noun phrase** is treated as an **uncountable noun**. It refers to a specific type of silence, one that is loud in its quietness due to its impact or significance. Since '**silence**' is uncountable, we don't necessarily need to use '**a**' necessarily before it. Therefore, we can say "or deafening silence" after "either a swift backlash".
 
• Interestingly, depending upon the context and stylistic choice of the writer, one could also use '**a'** before '**deafening silence'**. Both these versions would be grammatically correct.
 
 
• "They know they will face either a swift backlash or **a deafening silence."**
 
• "They know they will face either a swift backlash or** deafening silence."**
